title: Kolokolnikov's ACMAX conjecture
abstract: Proves that every simple graph on n ≥ 4 vertices with 2(n−2) edges has algebraic connectivity at most 2, attained by the complete bipartite graph K₂,ₙ₋₂. Develops Laplacian test-vector bounds, sparse cut certificates, and non-backtracking walk estimates used in the proof.

informal.ACMax.acmax_conjecture: For n ≥ 4, the algebraic connectivity of K₂,ₙ₋₂ is 2, and every simple graph on Fin n with exactly 2(n−2) edges has algebraic connectivity at most 2. Algebraic connectivity is the second-smallest eigenvalue of the combinatorial Laplacian, defined using Mathlib's ordered spectrum.
informal.ACMax.algConn_mul_sq_le: For a graph on any nonempty finite vertex type and any real vector whose coordinates sum to zero, algebraic connectivity times the squared norm is at most the Laplacian quadratic form.
informal.ACMax.algConn_le_two_of_testvector: A nonzero real vector with coordinate sum zero and Laplacian quadratic form at most twice its squared norm certifies algebraic connectivity at most 2.
informal.ACMax.algConn_completeBipartite_two: For n ≥ 4, the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes 2 and n−2 has algebraic connectivity exactly 2.
